use_case.name: coding
use_case.title: coding: an agent that fixes, runs and reviews code in its own sandbox
use_case.summary: A folder with a failing Python app, a skill with a script, a reviewer subagent and an AGENTS.md, deployed as a bundle. The agent's own E2B microVM does not exist until the first sandbox tool call makes it (and seeds it from the bundle); then it fixes the bug, reviews it, runs the app as a background job and looks at the page with a browser in the same VM.

tree.text:
---
name: reviewer
description: Reviews a small change to the app for correctness. Read-only; call it after you edit code, naming the file you changed.
tools: read, grep, find, ls
---

You are a careful, terse code reviewer for a small Python app. You can read files but not change them.

Read the file you are asked about and `app/test_server.py`. Check that the change does what the tests
expect and does not break anything obvious. Reply in at most four lines, then end with exactly one
last line, either

`REVIEWER-SIGNOFF: approved`

or `REVIEWER-SIGNOFF: changes-needed: <the reason>`.

---
model: gpt-5-mini
tools: read, edit, write, bash, bash_job, grep, find, ls, subagent, tool_search
max-steps: 40
---

You maintain a tiny Python web app in `app/` (standard library only: `app/server.py` and its tests in
`app/test_server.py`). The workspace is your working directory.

- To run the tests, use the `run-tests` skill: read its `SKILL.md` and run the script it names. Do not
  invent another way to run them.
- Fix bugs in `app/server.py`, never by editing the tests.
- After a change, have the `reviewer` agent review it before you say you are done, and report its
  `REVIEWER-SIGNOFF` line verbatim.
- Run the app with `bash` and `run_in_background=true` (it serves on port 8000). To look at a page it
  serves, use the browser tools, which you reach through `tool_search`; they run in the same machine,
  so `http://localhost:8000/` is the app.
- Keep your answers short: what you did, and what you saw.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run the app's unittest suite and end with a one-line verdict (see SKILL.md).
cd "$(dirname "$0")/../../../app" || exit 2
out=$(python3 -m unittest -v 2>&1)
status=$?
printf '%s\n' "$out"
ran=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n 's/^Ran \([0-9]*\) test.*/\1/p')
failed=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -c '\.\.\. FAIL$')
errors=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -c '\.\.\. ERROR$')
echo "RUN-TESTS-SKILL: ${ran:-0} run, $failed failed, $errors errors"
exit $status

---
name: run-tests
description: Run this project's test suite and get a one-line verdict. Use whenever you need to know whether the app's tests pass.
---

# Running the tests

Run the script from the workspace root:

```sh
bash .agents/skills/run-tests/run-tests.sh
```

It runs every test in `app/`, prints the unittest output, and ends with one line:

`RUN-TESTS-SKILL: <N> run, <F> failed, <E> errors`

Report that line. Exit status 0 means every test passed.
